original_question: Is the list packing number of every planar graph at most 7? That is, does chi*_l(G) <= 7 hold for every planar graph G?
target_in_paper: Section 2, subsection "Planar graphs", Problem 2.7: "Is it true that χ^⋆_ℓ(G) ≤ 7 for every planar graph?" ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.10046))
correct_elements: Your draft is essentially a restatement of the paper’s exact target. It has the correct graph class (planar graphs), the correct parameter (the list packing number χ^⋆_ℓ(G)), and the correct bound (7). It also uses the same universal quantifier structure as Problem 2.7. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.10046))
missing_details: The notation χ^⋆_ℓ(G) is not defined in the draft. In Section 2, the paper defines the list packing number as the least integer k such that G admits an L-packing of size k for every k-list-assignment L of G. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.10046))

To make the question stand-alone, you should define a k-list-assignment: a map L on V(G) assigning to each vertex a list of exactly k colors (the paper writes this as L: V(G) → (ℕ choose k)). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.10046))

You should define an L-colouring c of G: for each vertex v, the color c(v) must belong to L(v). The paper also separately specifies what it means for such a colouring to be proper: adjacent vertices receive different colors. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.10046))
You should define disjointness of colourings: two L-colourings c_i and c_j are disjoint if c_i(v) ≠ c_j(v) for every vertex v. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.10046))

To reflect the paper’s intended list-packing notion in a self-contained way, the question should say that one seeks k pairwise-disjoint proper L-colourings, not merely mention χ^⋆_ℓ(G) symbolically. This is the surrounding intent of the definitions and the planar-graph discussion. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.10046))

The scope should stay exactly at all planar graphs, with no extra hypotheses such as bipartite, triangle-free, cubic, bounded-degree, or higher-girth assumptions; those belong to neighboring problems, not Problem 2.7. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.10046))

If you want the question to be fully stand-alone, you may make explicit the standard ambient convention that G is a finite graph; this is implicit in the paper. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.10046))
refined_question: Is it true that every finite planar graph G satisfies χ^⋆_ℓ(G) ≤ 7, where χ^⋆_ℓ(G) denotes the least integer k such that for every k-list-assignment L: V(G) → {A ⊆ ℕ : |A| = k}, there exist k pairwise-disjoint proper L-colourings c_1, …, c_k of G, meaning that c_i(v) ∈ L(v) for every vertex v, adjacent vertices receive different colors in each c_i, and c_i(v) ≠ c_j(v) for every vertex v whenever i ≠ j? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.10046))
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Problem 2.7 in Section 2 under the subsection "Planar graphs". The paper introduces the needed notation earlier in the same section: list-assignments, L-colourings, disjointness, and χ^⋆_ℓ(G). The surrounding paragraph says only that recent papers improved upper bounds for planar graphs and asks whether those bounds can be improved further; it does not impose any extra restriction beyond planarity. So the sharp paper-faithful rewrite is simply Problem 2.7 with the definitions unpacked so that the question is self-contained. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.10046))
